Action Plan:
1. Begin prescribed medication as discussed: medication name not documented; instruct patient to take one tablet three times daily for 10 days. Prescription will be sent to Lloyds pharmacy (as per system). Note: route/dose name not fully documented.
2. Arrange an in-person review with a clinic doctor for ear examination, blood pressure measurement, assessment of gait and neurological function.
3. Safety advice: attend Emergency Department urgently if patient develops new weakness of arms/legs, sudden severe headache, or becomes violently vomitous.
4. Patient to contact support to book the in-person appointment.
5. Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

Subjective:
- Presenting complaint: acute dizziness/vertigo — room spinning, unsteady gait, ear buzzing, nausea.
- Onset/duration/progression:
  - Symptoms began approximately 2 hours prior to consult.
  - Similar, shorter episode about 1 month ago lasting ~5–10 minutes.
  - Current symptoms continuous over the past 2 hours.
- Associated symptoms:
  - Nausea; not vomited at time of consult.
  - Ear buzzing; no ear pain, no ear discharge.
  - No subjective hearing loss (hearing otherwise intact).
  - No fever reported.
  - No recent viral illness.
  - No weakness of arms or legs.
- Exacerbating/relieving factors: sudden onset while standing/making breakfast; not further specified.
- Past medical history:
  - Premature ovarian failure; has taken HRT.
- Medications: patient states none currently.
- Allergies: none reported.
- Social/contextual: patient ambulating at home but reports unsteadiness; lives with husband (was making husband breakfast when symptoms started).

Objective:
- No formal vitals recorded in transcript.
- No physical examination performed during the remote consult.
- Reported findings by patient:
  - Ambulatory but unsteady; room spinning.
  - Arms and legs functioning without weakness.
  - Ears buzzing; no pain or discharge; hearing intact.
- Planned in-person objective assessments (requested):
  - Ear examination (otoscopy).
  - Blood pressure measurement.
  - Observation of walking/gait and neurological exam.
- No investigations or imaging results documented.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Dizziness/vertigo:
   - Assessment: Labyrinthitis.
   - Differential diagnosis (applicable): Vestibular neuritis; benign paroxysmal positional vertigo (BPPV); central causes (e.g., cerebrovascular event) — consider if red flags present.
   - Investigations planned: In-person ear examination, blood pressure, gait/neurological assessment by clinic doctor. Further investigations (e.g., imaging, ENT referral) contingent on findings from in-person review.
   - Treatment planned:
     - Prescription sent to Lloyds pharmacy: medication name not documented; instructions given as one tablet three times daily for 10 days. (Route and exact medication name not documented.)
     - Symptomatic advice provided (rest, seek help if worsens).
   - Referrals planned: In-person review by clinic doctor; further referral (e.g., ENT) only if indicated after assessment.

Quality checks:
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - No recorded vital signs (blood pressure, pulse, temperature).
  - No physical examination findings documented (otoscopy, neurological exam).
  - Exact medication name and route not documented; dose frequency and duration partially documented (one tablet three times daily for ~10 days).
  - No documentation of antiemetic or analgesic prescription specifics.
- Internal conflicts from transcript:
  - Patient reported "premature ovarian failure" but doctor recorded/misheard as "premature hearing failure" — conflict noted.
- Transcript quality/comment:
  - Overall audible and coherent; minor inaudible segments and one mishearing by clinician as noted above. No objective examination or vital measurements were captured during the remote consult.
